recipes.name: Sara’s Sweet and Sour Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) can pineapple chunks, juice reserved
1 (8 ounce) can water chestnuts, drained and sliced
1.5 pounds cooked chicken meat, cut into strips

steps.text: Blend reserved pineapple juice, soy sauce, vinegar, and brown sugar in a 12-inch skillet or large saucepan over medium-low heat; mix in flour, and stir until thickened.
Stir in bell peppers, celery, and water chestnuts. Mix in cooked chicken and stir until heated through. Stir in pineapple chunks before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sara’s Sweet and Sour Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Sweet and sour chicken with pineapple, green peppers, celery, and water chestnuts in a soy, vinegar, and brown sugar sauce.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is really good, here's a little hint. Instead of the flour for the thickening, add about 2 tlbs. of cornstarch to 3/4 cup of ketchep, mix it up well until there are no lumps and pour the ketchep mixture in the hot sauce, it's thickens nicely and ketchup is a must in sweet and sour sauce I think. I added lots of chopped different colour peppers and onions. Yummy over rice.

Wowza! This is absolutely delish!!! I must admit, I was a bit skeptical at first.... I am NOT a fan of uncooked celery OR water chestnuts, but I was pleasantly surprised that I liked both in this! I pretty much followed Sal's directions to the letter except for a couple of substitutions. I had a red bell pepper to use up, so I added it (along with one green bell pepper). I cut all of my veggies (except the water chestnuts) into medium-sized chunks. Since my grocer was out of 20 oz. cans of pineapple in juice, I used almost all of (3) 8 oz. cans worth of fruit and juice. My final change was to sub 2 T cornstarch for the flour called for (I have never had any luck with flour as a thickener). NOTE #1: DO NOT add katsup to the sauce! I was tempted to (as a thickener and to impart some color), but I'm SOOOO glad I didn't. If you have red food coloring, use it instead. It only takes a few drops to turn your sauce a traditional red sweet & sour color and you won't have to compromise a great recipe to do so. NOTE #2: Be sure to whisk your thickener (flour or cornstarch) into your liquids BEFORE adding to your hot skillet. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring constantly until thickened and THEN turn the heat down and add your chicken / veggies. Other than needing more chicken (personal preference), I can't think of any way to improve upon this recipe. Just be sure to serve with plenty of rice to sop up the yummy sauce! Thanks for sharing your recipe, Sal. This is a winner for sure! :-)

The best homemade sweet and sour sauce I've ever made! I sauteed an onion, one green pepper and one red pepper first until the onion was cooked. Then added the ingredients to make the sauce, thickened it with cornstarch mixed with a bit of cold water, and finally added the cooked chicken (bought 8 large cooked and breaded filets from the hot deli section at the grocery store and sliced them up!) and the pineapple. It's a meal that's tasty, the right combo of sweet and tangy, and incredibly easy for week nights when you have no time!

Made this for company and my only changes were to stir fry the chicken first, otherwise it wouldn't be the least bit crispy. Then I also stir fried the veggies, added back the chicken and poured the sauce over and heated to thicken. Also added 1/2 cup of cashews (hubby loves). It was delicious and I will make again.

Yum! I really liked this recipe. Here is what I did: Cut up and cook the chicken and set it aside. Cut up the bell peppers as well as half an onion into chunks and cook them in the same pot as the chicken. Whisked together the liquids and 2 tablespoons of corn starch. When the vegetables were almost crisp tender, poured the freshly whisked liquid over the vegetables and stirred 1/2 cup of brown sugar. While the sauce started to thicken, I cut the chestnuts in half and added them and the chicken to the pot. When the sauce was just about the right thickness, dumped in the pineapple. Note: I used coconut aminos instead of soy sauce. Served over a wild rice blend. Delicious!

This was so easy, versatile and good! It is as delicious as any restaurant dish.....REALLY! I very quickly stir fried some onion, broccoli, thinly sliced carrots and peppers once the sauce was done and the chicken was browned and cooked through. Then I added veggies and served over rice before they got soft. To the sauce I added about 1/4 tsp each of minced garlic and ginger, and a squirt of ketchup. I thickened the sauce with cornstarch. Mmmm mmm good. Use pork or even store bought meatballs.

I used fresh broccoli in place of the water chestnuts because my husband doesn't like them I steamed them for 2 minutes first. My prep time was quite a bit longer since I had to cut up everything, but it was worth the wait!

Turned out great! Definitely a keeper! My only adjustment was adding a quartered onion and sauteing vegetables with fresh ginger root (later removed) and fresh minced garlic before adding them to the sauce. I used cornstarch, instead of flour and let the sauce reduce a little bit with the piece of ginger root that I later removed.

This was very good! I made a half recipe, using frozen multi-colored pepper strips that I had on hand (would increase the amount the next time). Per some of the recommendations, I used corn starch in place of the flour, dissolving it an equal amount of ketchup. I did find the celery to be a little hard, so also next time, I would saute the celery for a few minutes beforehand, maybe adding some onion slices, as well. I used apple cider vinegar and also added garlic and onion powder. Skipped the water chestnuts because I don't usually have them on hand. Served with jasmine rice that I made in my rice cooker. Thanks for the great recipe, Sal, that came together fairly quickly.

Today I made the recipe and my family and I enjoyed this delicious and heavenly dish!! I read other reviews. I just only added 1/2 cup of ketcup and reduced down to 1/2 cup of celery. I followed all these ingredients. The sauce became thickened!. I grilled the chicken before I chopped them and stirred them in the sauce sauepan. It smelled so sweet! Next time I will make half of floured chicken and grilled chicken separately because my 5-year-old girl wanted the floured chicken. The sauce tasted the exact flavor from Chopsticks restarant!! That is what I desperately looked for many many many years!! Thank you very much, Sal!!! This recipe is in my box!! You should win this recipe!

This is Wonderful!! I cubed the chicken and sauteed it in sesame oil. Based on the 1st review I mixed 2 T. cornstarch in 3/4 C. ketchup and use that as a thickening agent instead of the 1/4 C. flour. Used green and orange bell pepper. Will try adding unsalted cashews next time.

So simple and so delicious! I substituted tofu in place of the chicken - cut into bite-sized pieces, dusted with cornstarch and stir fried with garlic to get it crispy. Like other folks I added some onion and then very briefly put the other veggies (I used orange pepper, celery, and snow peas) in the stir fry pan before adding the tofu, veggies, pineapple, and cashews to the pan of sauce. Definitely a keeper!
I made pretty much as recipe stated. I did not have the water chestnuts. I used a little less vinegar & sugar. I used frozen pepper onion mix. Sauce thickened very nicely. Served over rice.
Perfect balance of sweet and sour! I used red pepper for one half of the green pepper ingredient simply to give it some color pop! This one goes into my actual card file! Thank you!
I didn’t have the water chestnuts but it was still delicious and so fast and easy.
Way too much vinegar for our tastes. Next time I'll use less. I also added ketchup and more brown sugar to try to help the strong vinegar taste.

I used the original recipe. It is very sweet but I loved it. I used rice vinegar. I also cooked my chicken in sesame seed oil then added the peppers and celery and cooked them. I’ll definitely make this again because it was so quick and easy.

I will use less brown sugar next time as it was a little too sweet for our liking. Also, we used broccoli instead of celery as that is what we had in the fridge. Hubby says make again so that means it was good!
